info.title: CheckAnySite API
info.summary: What is this website? Evidence about any site: AI builders, popularity, technology, trust signals.
info.description:
Ask what we found about any public website, each finding with its evidence and source. Free during launch: every account gets 300 credits a month, and more on request; each key may make 60 requests every 60 seconds, and every answer says how many are left (`X-RateLimit-*`).

Two APIs, one key: GET reads our stored results and never scans (the Lookup API); POST scans (the Scan API), and takes an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry never scans or charges twice.

Docs: https://docs.checkanysite.com/. Errors: https://docs.checkanysite.com/errors.

Within v1 fields and values may be added, never removed or renamed: ignore what you don’t know.

get.description:
The Lookup API: our newest stored result for a site, however old, that answers the checks asked (every check when `checks` is left out). It holds those checks; the other fields are null. It never scans: check `scannedAt`, ask `maxAgeDays` for a fresher one, and scan with POST /scans. Each answer has an ETag: send it back in `If-None-Match` and, while the answer is the same, you get a 304 with no body, free.

Credits: Each check asked at its stored price, at most 3 (every check), when a result is found; nothing for no_result or a 304.

parameters.name: checks
parameters.description: The checks to answer, separated by commas; left out, every check.

parameters.name: maxAgeDays
parameters.description: Answer only with a result at most this many days old (1 to 3650); otherwise `no_result`.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of the answer you hold: while it is unchanged, the answer is a 304 with no body, free.

304.description: The answer is the one whose `ETag` you sent: no body, no credits.

400.description: `invalid_domain`: The address isn’t a public domain name we can look up (an IP address, a private name, a typo). `invalid_parameter`: A parameter is missing, unknown or has a value the API doesn’t accept; `param` names it.

401.description: `missing_api_key`: The request carries no API key. `invalid_api_key`: The API key isn’t one of ours, or has a typo in it. `revoked_api_key`: The API key was revoked by its owner and no longer works. `expired_api_key`: The API key has passed its expiry date: the one it was made with, or the end of its grace period after it was rotated.

404.description: `no_result`: We have no result for this site that answers the question, or none as recent as asked.

429.description: `rate_limited`: This key made more requests than its rate limit allows in a short window. `quota_exceeded`: The account has used its credits for this month. `key_limit_reached`: This key has used the monthly credits its owner allowed it.

500.description: `internal_error`: Something went wrong on our side. No credits were used.

post.description:
The Lookup API for up to 50 domains at once: each domain’s stored result, as GET /sites/{domain} gives it, or why there is none, in the order sent. A domain sent twice is answered once; one we have no result for, or that isn’t a domain, gets an `error` in its place, and the others are answered. It never scans.

Credits: Each result found at its checks’ stored price, at most 3 each; misses are free. A batch is charged whole: when the credits don’t cover every result found, it is refused and nothing is charged.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value for this request, such as a UUID: a retry with the same key within 24 hours gets the first answer again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`), never a second scan or charge. The same key with another request is `idempotency_key_reused`.

200.description: A result or an error for each domain.

400.description: `invalid_json`: The request body couldn’t be read as a JSON object. `invalid_parameter`: A parameter is missing, unknown or has a value the API doesn’t accept; `param` names it.

401.description: `missing_api_key`: The request carries no API key. `invalid_api_key`: The API key isn’t one of ours, or has a typo in it. `revoked_api_key`: The API key was revoked by its owner and no longer works. `expired_api_key`: The API key has passed its expiry date: the one it was made with, or the end of its grace period after it was rotated.

409.description: `idempotency_key_in_use`: A request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still being answered.

413.description: `request_too_large`: The request body is larger than the API reads.

415.description: `unsupported_media_type`: The request body has a content type other than JSON.

422.description: `idempotency_key_reused`: This `Idempotency-Key` came with a different request in the last day; a key stands for one request.

429.description: `rate_limited`: This key made more requests than its rate limit allows in a short window. `quota_exceeded`: The account has used its credits for this month. `key_limit_reached`: This key has used the monthly credits its owner allowed it.

500.description: `internal_error`: Something went wrong on our side. No credits were used.

post.description:
Answers from a result scanned in the last day when one answers the checks asked (200), joins a scan of the site already running (202), or starts a new scan (202). Poll the scan’s `links.self` until `complete` is true; the first answers come in seconds, slow sources fill in after. A scan runs only what the checks asked need, so a few checks are faster and cost less than every check. A read-only key gets a recent result or a running scan, never a new one (`read_only_key`). To check a fix, ask the `readiness` check with `again: true`: once its answer is a few minutes old, it is asked again.

Credits: Each check asked at its scan price, at most 15 (every check), for a new scan; at its stored price, at most 3, when a recent result or a running scan answers.

parameters.description: A unique value for this request, such as a UUID: a retry with the same key within 24 hours gets the first answer again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`), never a second scan or charge. The same key with another request is `idempotency_key_reused`.

post.description:
The Scan API for up to 10 domains at once: each domain as POST /scans answers it (a recent result, a running scan, or a new one), in the order sent. A domain the credits, the cap or our rules refuse gets an `error` in its place; the others go on. Poll each scan’s `links.self`.

Credits: Each domain as POST /scans charges it: its checks’ scan price for a new scan, their stored price for a recent result or a running scan. Each scan’s credits are counted before the next.

get.description:
A scan’s status, and its result once completed, holding the checks asked: poll the scan’s `links.self`, which names them. `complete` turns true when the scan failed, or completed with every slow source in; until then the `Retry-After` header says when to ask again.

Credits: Free.

parameters.name: checks
parameters.description: The checks its result holds, as the scan was asked; `links.self` names them.

200.description: The scan as it is now.

400.description: `invalid_parameter`: A parameter is missing, unknown or has a value the API doesn’t accept; `param` names it.

401.description: `missing_api_key`: The request carries no API key. `invalid_api_key`: The API key isn’t one of ours, or has a typo in it. `revoked_api_key`: The API key was revoked by its owner and no longer works. `expired_api_key`: The API key has passed its expiry date: the one it was made with, or the end of its grace period after it was rotated.

404.description: `scan_not_found`: There is no scan with this id.

410.description: `scan_expired`: This scan is older than the results we keep, so its result is gone; the site’s newest result is kept.

headerKey.name: X-API-Key
headerKey.description: The same key, in its own header.

RequestId.description: This request’s id; give it when you write to us.

CreditsCost.description: Credits this call cost (only on calls that cost credits).

CreditsRemaining.description: Credits the account has left this month after this call.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests the key may make per window (60 seconds).

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests the key has left in the current window, this one counted.

RateLimitReset.description: When the current window ends, in Unix seconds.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before asking again.

ETag.description: This answer’s tag: send it in `If-None-Match` to get a free 304 while it is unchanged.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this is the first answer to an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

Evidence.description: Where a finding was seen, with the exact text: the reason it is reported.

where.description: Where we saw it: "index.html, line 14", "response header", "address".

snippet.description: The element, header or excerpt as it appears.

match.description: The part of the snippet that matched.

masked.description: True when email addresses and phone numbers in the snippet are masked.

AiTraces.description: Traces of the AI website builders and patterns we found. Evidence, never a verdict about who made the site.

level.description: `high`: an AI builder’s own trace; `medium`: a combination of its weaker traces only; `none`: no traces found.

kind.description: `ai` for AI builders, `general` for other site builders.

strength.description: `signature`: one trace of its own; `combination`: weaker traces that count only together.

combination.description: For a combination, what its traces mean together.

evidence.description: Where each trace was seen, with the exact line.

builders.description: Each builder whose traces we found; empty when none.

note.description: Why it is weak evidence on its own.

patterns.description: Design patterns common on AI-built pages; they never set the level on their own.

AiReadiness.description: How easily AI tools can find, read and use the site: a score out of 100 from checks, each with its evidence, and what to fix first. What the site lets AI crawlers do is listed apart and never scored: keeping AI out is the site’s choice.

answer.description: The answer in a sentence ("Ready for AI: it scores 82 of 100.").

note.description: What it lets AI crawlers do, in a sentence: the site’s choice, never scored.

score.description: Out of 100; null when too little could be checked to say.

checkedAt.description: When AI access was checked: the scan’s own date, or for a result made before we checked AI access, the newer check that answers in its place.

meaning.description: What reaching it means, in a sentence.

level.description: The highest level it reaches; null when it reaches none.

reached.description: True when the site reaches it.

levels.description: Every level, lowest first; one counts once its checks and every level before it are met.

needs.description: The keys of the checks it still needs, as `checks` lists them.

next.description: The first level not reached and what it needs; null once every level is.

comparison.description: Where the score stands among the most visited sites we read, in a sentence; null without a score.

partial.description: True when some checks couldn’t be made or are still checking; the rest is scaled to 100.

key.description: A stable key: `text`, `listing`, `facts`, `structured`, `sitemap`, `robots`, `agents` (every file for AI agents at once: one found is enough), `llms`, `links` or `markdown`; new keys may appear.

group.description: `find` (can AI find its pages?), `read` (can AI read it?) or `agents` (can agents use it?).

evidence.description: Where it was seen, with the exact line.

met.description: True when it earns its full points.

unchecked.description: True when we couldn’t check it, or it is still checking: it is left out of the score.

optional.description: True for what few sites have yet; it is worth few points.

gain.description: The points fixing it would add to the score.

todo.description: What to do, in a line.

prompt.description: A prompt for an AI coding assistant to fix it, with the site’s address and what we found.

fix.description: What to do about it; null when it is met or couldn’t be checked.

checks.description: Each check that counts, as the score reads it.

fixPrompt.description: The fixes that aren’t optional, most points first, as one prompt for an AI coding assistant that ends with where to check again; the optional ones once only they are left. Null when there is nothing to fix.

name.description: The crawler, as its maker writes it ("GPTBot").

company.description: The AI company it belongs to, for those we follow.

role.description: What it fetches pages for: `training` models, or `answers` (AI assistants and AI search).

access.description: `out` of the whole site, kept from `some` paths, or let `in`.

line.description: The robots.txt line of the group that decides it; null when no group names it.

crawlers.description: Every AI crawler we know, as the site’s robots.txt treats it; never scored.

Popularity.description: How popular the site is, from public ranked lists: a band and each list’s rank, never a visit count.

band.description: The best band any list gives the site ("Top 100K"), or "Outside top 1M".

bestRank.description: The best rank behind the band; null when no list ranks the site.

rank.description: The rank, or null when the list doesn’t rank the site.

isBucket.description: True when the rank is the edge of a bucket, not an exact position.

rankedAs.description: The parent name the list ranks, when not the site itself.

asOf.description: When the list was produced, as it states it.

license.description: The list’s license, when its terms ask for attribution: keep it when you republish.

ranks.description: Each list we read, with the site’s rank on it.

Technology.description: The technologies the site shows, each with its evidence, and the network announcing its address.

evidence.description: Where it was seen, with the exact line.

technologies.description: Each technology the site shows, with its evidence.

asn.description: The autonomous system number, such as 13335.

name.description: The organisation announcing the address ("Cloudflare, Inc.").

prefix.description: The routed block holding the address ("104.16.16.0/20").

network.description: A network, never a place: many networks answer from everywhere.

DnsRecords.description: The domain’s DNS records as the scan read them, over DNS over HTTPS, and the network announcing its address.

read.description: False when the lookup failed: then there are no records to give.

name.description: The name asked about: the domain, its www host, or a policy entry such as `_dmarc`.

type.description: The record type. SVCB and HTTPS come only from `_agents`, where a site names its AI agents.

value.description: The record’s value, as the resolver gave it.

dnssec.description: Whether the resolver validated the answer with DNSSEC; null when that didn’t answer.

incomplete.description: The questions ("example.com TXT") that didn’t answer whole: a record missing from one of them may still exist.

asn.description: The autonomous system number, such as 13335.

name.description: The organisation announcing the address ("Cloudflare, Inc.").

prefix.description: The routed block holding the address ("104.16.16.0/20").

network.description: The network announcing the site’s address, never a place.

TrustSignals.description: Signals about how established and reachable the site is. Signals, never a verdict.

key.description: A stable key such as `privacyPolicy` or `domainAge`; new keys may appear.

state.description: `found`, `partial`, `none` (not found; absence is never an accusation), `info` (a fact) or `unknown` (couldn’t check).

kind.description: `measured` by us, `sourced` from a named source, or `interpreted` from what we read.

source.description: Where it came from: our scan or a named source.

evidence.description: Where it was seen, when the page or a record shows it.

pending.description: True while a slow source is still being read.

checks.description: Each signal we looked for, found or not.

Score.description: A score out of 100 for how established the site looks, from its parts; it says nothing about intent.

total.description: Out of 100; null when too little could be read to score fairly.

band.description: The band the total falls in.

withheld.description: True when too little could be read; `total` is null then.

max.description: The most it could earn from what we could check.

reasons.description: Why points were given or withheld, one short phrase each.

checked.description: False when none of its inputs could be checked.

parts.description: The parts the total is made of, each with its points.

missing.description: Inputs we couldn’t check; the rest is scaled to 100.

SiteSummary.description: What the site is: its own words, its kind, an automatic summary, who is behind it and its profiles.

siteName.description: The name the site gives itself.

kind.description: The kind of site we read it as (a shop, a blog, an app…); null when unclear.

text.description: Two or three sentences: what the site is and offers, as the page presents it.

category.description: What kind of site the model read it as.

offerings.description: What it offers, in short phrases.

audience.description: Who it is for, when the page says.

summary.description: An automatic summary whose quotes we checked against the page; null when there is none.

name.description: The name as the source gives it.

source.description: Where it comes from: `structured data`, `copyright line`, `Wikidata` or `certificate`.

names.description: Each name a source gives for who is behind the site.

agreeing.description: The sources whose names agree, when at least two do.

identity.description: Who is behind the site, by independent sources.

inceptionYear.description: The year it was founded or launched.

handle.description: The account as its address names it ("acme", "company/acme").

noai.description: True when a `noai` robots tag or header is set.

summary.description: The summary it writes for AI assistants.

firstSeen.description: The earliest certificate’s start date; null when there were too many to read.

firstCertificate.description: Certificate Transparency: when a certificate for the domain was first issued.

domain.description: The site’s domain, as we read it ("example.com").

limited.description: Set when the page itself couldn’t be read; the result then comes from outside records.

finalUrl.description: The address the scan ended at, after redirects.

resultUrl.description: The result on our site, with every section and its evidence.

versions.description: The signature list and score formula the result was made with (/changelog).
